newsitem.title: JAPAN: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - March 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - March 6.

text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in the Japanese press on Thursday, as reported by Kyodo news agency:
-- Lower House approves 77 trillion yen 1997/98 budget without amendment.
-- Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) calls for scrapping securities transaction tax by the end of March 1999 under Japan's "Big Bang" plan for deregulation of financial markets.
-- Oil dealer Izui spent 170 million yen wining and dining central government bureaucrats over four-year period.
-- Japanese ambassador to Cuba has informal meeting with Cuban President Fidel Castro to seek help from Cuba to solve hostage crisis in Lima.
-- A joint U.S.-South Korea briefing for North Korea on proposal for four-party peace talks on Korean peninsula held on Wednesday.
-- Another strong earthquake hits Izu Peninsula with intensity in the city of Ito measuring nearly five on the Japanese scale.
-- Japanese embassy staff in Lebanon meet detained Red Army members.
